decision: goal: iOS alpha of else.bot that only connects to remote servers, built on NSH
why: user asked for a mobile version for the morning; remote only, iOS first

decision: proved NSH Rust app builds and runs on the iOS simulator before writing app code
why: biggest unknown was the toolchain; hello app packaged in 3 min

decision: Rust NSH app (not TSX) in apps/mobile, own cargo workspace, reusing crates/wire
why: reuses the server's wire types and the desktop's client rules; NSH builds its own runners so it stays out of the root workspace

decision: own tokio+reqwest+tungstenite client instead of NSH fetch/websocket
why: NSH fetch follows redirects; the desktop refuses them so the owner key never leaves the saved origin; same TLS verification

decision: cross-compiled aws-lc rustls reqwest tungstenite for aarch64-apple-ios-sim
why: TLS C code was the second biggest unknown

decision: http:// only to loopback or Tailscale IPs, and only when the phone has a Tailscale interface address
why: iOS cannot run tailscale status like the desktop; a 100.x address with Tailscale off could route to carrier CGNAT

decision: dev server via scripts/dev.py with every real provider CLI pointed at /nonexistent
why: host_providers would let codex run real turns on the owner's account; only synthetic may run

decision: connect, wrong-key error, bot list, chat, send and live reply checked on the simulator against the dev server
why: the predicate is the real app on iOS against a real server
evidence: iPhone 18 Pro sim screenshots this session

decision: bot replies full width without a bubble, owner messages as bubbles
why: tables and code blocks collapsed inside a content-sized bubble; long Markdown reads better full width as in ChatGPT and Claude iOS

decision: keyboard_taps Handled on the transcript and the connect form
why: the first tap on Send or Connect only dismissed the keyboard
evidence: sim: sent with keyboard up in one tap

decision: question and draft cards in the chat; answered/discarded receipts after the turn
why: a phone is where you answer a waiting bot; replying is the main reason to open the app
evidence: sim: answered a question (db answer=dentist), discarded a draft (status=discarded)

decision: Send on a draft asks for confirmation first and sends exactly the shown version
why: it emails or messages someone in the owner's name and cannot be undone

decision: seeded a pending question and an email draft straight into the disposable dev sqlite
why: only the provider's per-turn token can create them through the API; no mail account is connected so nothing can send

decision: stop, failure and interrupted states checked with synthetic hang and fail
why: stop must reach the server and the owner must tell their own stop from a failure
evidence: turn status interrupted via API; sim screenshot

decision: owner key in the iOS Keychain; app storage only when the build has no Keychain group
why: keep the key out of app files and backups; the simulator package has no entitlement and hardcoding a group needs the user's team id
evidence: sim: keychain refused -34018, fell back, profile survived relaunch

decision: Sol high review: 3 P1, 4 P2; fixed all
why: independent review from the other model family, as the repo's model policy asks for Claude-written code

decision: draft card shows Cc, Bcc and attachments before Send
why: the owner must see everything Send delivers

decision: Tailscale check counts only addresses on utun interfaces
why: a carrier can assign 100.64/10 on pdp_ip; that must not unlock plain http

decision: Keychain item AfterFirstUnlockThisDeviceOnly; purge the old JSON profile
why: keep the key out of backups and other devices

decision: Chat::Recovering state; reload retries with backoff while the chat is open
why: a failed reload after a gap left the chat frozen past the stream cursor

decision: unknown-outcome retry reuses the request id only for unchanged text; HTTP receipt never overwrites streamed state
why: edited text with the old id would get request_conflict; a late response could regress a turn

decision: read marking only once loaded, no stuck in-flight flag; card errors use the server's message and an explicit unknown state
why: an effect re-run cancelled the task and left the flag set forever

decision: did not push: pre-push suite has 8 else-api failures on macOS
why: the same tests fail on base 8d7cfc5a (macOS /private/var paths, Linux process groups); repo rules forbid --no-verify
evidence: nextest on a base worktree: 3/3 failed

decision: goal 2: drafts editing, secret requests, attachments, creating bots, several servers, one commit each
why: user asked for them after the alpha

decision: draft edit saves through PUT at the version shown, then the live update redraws the card; Send stays on the saved version
why: matches the server lifecycle; no unsaved edits ride on an approval
evidence: sim: body edited, DB version 1 to 2, card shows new text

decision: secret requests: card with one field per variable, masked unless the name ends in USER, EMAIL, HOST and similar; Decline or Save; settled ones leave a receipt
why: unblocks a bot that waits on credentials from the phone
evidence: sim: seeded request, saved, DB stored + vault entry with both names, receipt shown

decision: attachments: + opens Photo Library or Choose File; each pick uploads at once with its own id, Send names the uploaded files as parts after the text; owner messages show photos as thumbnails and files as chips, fetched with the key into tmp, tap opens the share sheet
why: mirrors the desktop upload and parts contract; reqwest keeps the one-origin rule for downloads
evidence: sim: logo.png and notes.txt sent, DB parts match, thumbnail shown, share sheet opened; photo library broken in this simulator (Unable to Load Photos, addmedia 3301)

decision: creating bots: Compose in the list header opens New Bot (name, color, live avatar); the create request keeps its request_id after an unknown outcome; success opens the new chat
why: the server dedups creates by request_id
evidence: sim: Travel Planner created (DB pink), chat opened, back lands on the list

decision: the create request runs in a screen effect, not in the header button handler
why: NSH spawn ends with its owner; the reactive header rebuilt on the label change and cancelled the request, leaving Creating… forever

decision: several servers: a saved list (Storage servers, active in server-origin, keys per origin in the vault); More menu lists them with a check, switches, Add Server reuses the connect form, Disconnect removes only the current one and opens the next
why: the root is keyed on the Link value so a switch rebuilds the stack and ends the old live connection; launch no longer rewrites the key
evidence: sim: added a 2nd dev server, switched both ways, sent after switch, relaunch kept the active one, disconnect fell back to the other

decision: commits 57a56173 (secret handling) and d64c79c4 (durable profile identity) are risky per pstack-models; built by Opus in this session, reviewed by Sol high
why: routing policy

decision: Sol review: secrets always masked and cleared on submit; file cache scoped by server and bot and evicted on disconnect; attach notices apart from the send state; retry IDs keyed on the full message and on name plus avatar; mutations held by the server session (spawn_held + try_set) so cards, buttons and screens can go away; unknown card outcomes retriable; failed uploads keep bytes and retry under the same ID with server metadata; forget writes the list before removing the key; launch falls back to another saved server; neutral receipt for a cancelled secret request
why: 9 findings, 3 high
evidence: sim: decline receipt, draft v3, photo send, bot create all after the fixes; cargo test 18 pass, clippy clean

decision: not done: applying the HTTP receipt on success and refetching on an unknown card outcome (live update covers success; unknown is now retriable); a create still unresolved after leaving New Bot is not shown again
why: low impact for the alpha

decision: next: iOS icon from the macOS tile, shaped avatars, sending a draft after its turn ended, choosing a bot's provider and model
why: user asked; scroll overshoot filed upstream as longbridge/nsh#2901 for later

decision: iOS icon is a new source media/branding/else-bot-ios.svg (the macOS tile square and full bleed) rendered by scripts/generate-icons.py, flattened to RGB
why: iOS masks corners itself and refuses alpha; one script keeps every icon generated from source
evidence: icon PNG viewed; local rsvg matches the committed PNGs, its icns differs (Pillow) so the committed icns is kept

decision: avatar geometry moves from apps/desktop/src/avatar.rs to else_wire::avatar; mobile draws it as inline SVG through NSH svg()
why: one table for both apps instead of a copy that drifts; NSH iOS enables svg by default
evidence: workspace clippy clean; avatar tests pass; sim: list and New Bot pickers drawn

decision: a draft whose turn ended is sent by an owner reply carrying open_draft ('Send it as it is.'), request ID uuid v5 of draft id and version; every composer message also carries the open draft, as the desktop does
why: the server lets the Approve button act only while the drafting turn runs (can_approve); the desktop tags such drafts 'Reply in chat' and the bot confirms with confirm_draft_approval; v5 keeps the ID stable when the card is rebuilt by the virtual list
evidence: sim: Send on the Inbox email draft posted the reply with the draft; DB context_turn set, then discarded by 0037 because the synthetic bot never confirms; real confirm path not exercised (needs a model provider)

decision: provider and model: a Model screen in each chat (GET/PUT /v1/bots/{id}/profile) and a Model row in New Bot that sends the profile with POST /v1/bots, only when it differs from the defaults; desktop's catalog_choice moves to ProviderInfo::choice in else-wire with effort_label and FAST_TIER
why: the server takes a profile at creation, so no second request; a bot without its own profile keeps following the defaults; one picking rule for both apps
evidence: sim against a server with a stub claude CLI: saved Sonnet 5.5 High for Inbox (bot_profiles row), reopened shows it with Save disabled; created Haiku Helper with Haiku 5.5 Medium in one request; unavailable providers show the server's reason; wire tests moved and pass

decision: 7f73dfbc (owner approval of an external send) and 8639836c (the profile that runs a bot, durable create identity) are risky per pstack-models; written by Opus in this session, reviewed by Sol high
why: routing policy; Sol agreed on 7f73dfbc and added 8639836c

decision: Sol review: the composer no longer attaches the open draft (only the card's Send does), so ordinary chat cannot close a draft, rebind its approval reply, change a retry's identity, or fail on a stale version; Model Save compares with the profile the bot uses now (own or followed); an unavailable provider's options are read-only and a provider the server dropped opens with nothing picked and a note; New Bot compares with the raw defaults; an unknown profile save keeps what it tried and reads the profile back before saving again, refusing if it changed elsewhere
why: 2 high, 4 medium findings
evidence: sim: Save disabled on an unchanged own profile, enabled after picking Low; cargo test 19 pass, clippy clean

decision: not done: the server's PUT /v1/bots/{id}/profile has no revision precondition, so a save from two devices racing still ends last-write-wins (the client now detects a change made before its retry); no API test for the chat approval of a draft whose turn ended
why: server change, outside the mobile scope

decision: a Details screen behind an info button in the chat header replaces the Model button: model, rules, routines, reminders, watching, triggers, read-only; lists come from the open chat's snapshot extras and bot.updated; rules from GET /v1/bots/{id}/rules, reloaded when rules_version changes; schedule wording moves from the desktop to else_wire::schedule
why: user asked for the desktop's right panel on the phone; the snapshot already carries the lists, so no new endpoint; one schedule wording for both apps
evidence: sim with sample rows: routines (one paused), reminder, webhook, empty Watching; saving Opus from Model updated the Details row; workspace clippy clean, wire tests pass

decision: not done: acting on routines and triggers from the phone (pause, retry, delete, stop a watcher), usage, rule history and restore
why: read-only first pass; the desktop keeps those actions

decision: Sol review of ab2383ed (routine): routines and reminders show the desktop's last-run line (skipped, failed, retrying, paused and why) and their time zone, from Routine::schedule/next_run/last_run_line moved to else_wire::schedule; watchers show the last check and the next one (helpers moved too); webhooks show their pace and every trigger its last wake; the model and rules are read again after bot.updated, on reconnect, and when Details is back on top (an owner's change from another device sends no event); the Model row always opens the picker; the Rules page renders the shared read; the lists say Loading, the load error, or Updating instead of looking empty; session::load and load_older recheck the chat after their request (pre-existing panic on a closed chat)
why: 5 medium, 2 low, 1 pre-existing
evidence: sim: time zones, pace and pause reason shown; a model changed by API showed after returning from Model; workspace clippy clean; wire and desktop tests pass; mobile 20 pass

decision: the desktop's client (api, live, endpoints, origin and token, conversation model) moves to a new crates/client (else-client); the phone uses it instead of its fork, keeping only its runtime, Tailscale check (Client::with_tailnet), message composition and transcript projection
why: thermo-nuclear review (Fable 5.2 medium): the fork had drifted (unknown-outcome rule, no time zone on sends, bot_deleted folded into reset, no secret description, question answers that could be empty); one client means one fix
evidence: desktop 684 tests pass on the crate; workspace clippy clean; mobile 14 tests; sim: bot list, send, live turn update all through the shared client

decision: the earlier reason for not using NSH networking (NSH fetch follows redirects) is out of date: HttpRequest.follow_redirects exists in nsh-core 0.6.1. reqwest stays because it is what makes the client shareable with the desktop
why: review finding 1.1
